title: Hybrid row virtualization (variable-height) + focus-anchored column handles + density token migration
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Context: Our current table virtualization assumes fixed row height which breaks for mixed-content cells (multi-line comments, badges, inline charts). This causes jank during scroll and incorrect focus restoration when rows above change height. We need a hybrid virtualization strategy that supports variable-height rows while keeping memory and CPU predictable. At the same time, we should introduce a focus-anchored column handle (keyboard and pointer-friendly) and migrate density-related spacing to new design tokens so other components can reuse them.

Goals:
- Implement hybrid virtualization (pixel + item) to support variable-height rows with minimal reflow and stable focus.
- Design a focus-anchored column drag handle: visible on focus/hover, keyboard operable, with clear hit target and motion affordance.
- Introduce a small set of density tokens (density-compact/comfortable/relaxed) and map existing table spacing tokens to them.
- Provide design specs, accessibility guidance, and interaction prototypes for engineering.

Non-goals:
- Full rewrite of the table renderer. We will implement adapters for the current virtual list runtime.
- Supporting arbitrarily tall rows without limits; we will set guidelines for max variable height to maintain performance.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prototype demonstrates smooth scroll with mixed-height rows on a dataset of 50k rows in dev harness.
- Focus/selection persists correctly when rows above change height and after pagination/insert/delete operations.
- Column handle visible on keyboard focus, provides aria-label/descriptions, supports left/right arrow nudging and drag-to-resize with snap points.
- Density tokens added to tokens.json and documented; table demos show three density presets and a migration guide for apps.
- Design specs include token values, motion timings, hit-target sizes, and QA checklist.

Design notes and decisions:
- Hybrid virtualization approach: keep coarse item indexing for large jumps, use a pixel-offset cache for recent windows. On measured row-height changes, update cache incrementally rather than recomputing whole layout.
- Use a sentinel-based measurement window (200 rows around viewport) to amortize remeasurement cost.
- Column handle: anchor to header cell's right edge; when focused, show a 20x44px hit region (to meet a11y); visible indicator for draggable state; keyboard interaction supports +/- 8px nudges and shift for 32px.
- Density token mapping: introduce tokens "density-compact-spacing", "density-default-spacing", "density-relaxed-spacing" and map existing padding/margin tokens in table component to them. Leave other components optional to migrate later.

API/implementation suggestions for engineers:
- Table props: variableRowSupport: "hybrid" | "fixed"; measurementWindow: integer; density: "compact" | "default" | "relaxed"; columnHandle: { enabled: boolean, keyboardStep: number }.
- Provide a measuredRowHeight cache with validation TTL to avoid stale sizes after remote content loads (images / charts).

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Remeasure storms when many rows change simultaneously (bulk updates). Mitigation: debounce layout updates, batch apply measurements, and provide a fallback to fixed mode.
- Risk: Performance regressions on low-end devices. Mitigation: telemetry gating (only enable hybrid by default on supported devices/flags) and a developer toggle to revert to fixed-height rendering.

Deliverables:
- Figma frames (header handles, row measurement overlay, density token page).
- Interactive prototype (Chromium) showing 50k mixed rows.
- Tokens PR and console docs.
- Engineering handoff doc with pseudocode and measurement guidelines.
